title: Three-color triangles
notes: On another visit, K-1 can move a single all-three cell (P5), optimize the subdivided board (P4), or change the boundary rule (P6). Grades 2-3 can return to the local door cases and two-color rows (P3-4) before the impossibility argument (P5-6). Grades 4-5 can keep their minimum/maximum fillings and build the parity explanation (P3-5), with P6 as a separate test of the boundary hypothesis. A first visit ending with a well-checked filling leaves substantial mathematics for the next.

For four K-1 children, prepare four sets of fifteen counters in each of R, B and Y: 180 counters altogether. Two shared pair sets need 90. Keep the prescribed counter size and print scale; actual stock fit remains untested.
